content: Certain medications can influence the blood levels of omeprazole, and omeprazole can also affect the blood levels of other medications. It is essential to inform your healthcare provider about all the medications you are currently taking or have recently taken. This includes prescription drugs, over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and other supplements. Omeprazole may interfere with the absorption of some medications, so it is crucial to discuss your full medication list with your healthcare provider. Note that this may not be an exhaustive list of potential drug interactions with omeprazole. If you or someone else has accidentally taken too much omeprazole, seek immediate medical attention. You should call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of omeprazole, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose or extra doses to make up for the missed one. Omeprazole should be taken before meals. It is unclear whether alcohol consumption affects the efficacy or safety of omeprazole. Always inform your healthcare provider about any prescription or OTC medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are using. Specifically, let your healthcare provider know if you are taking any of the following medications before starting omeprazole: Clopidogrel (Plavix): A blood thinner used to prevent or treat blood clots. Cilostazol (Pletal): A medication used to alleviate symptoms of intermittent claudication. Citalopram: A medication used to treat depression. Methotrexate (Trexall and others): A drug used for certain cancers, autoimmune diseases, or other conditions. Digoxin (Lanoxin): A medication used to treat irregular heartbeats and some types of heart failure. Warfarin: A blood thinner. Certain antiretroviral medications (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir) used for HIV or AIDS. St. John’s Wort: A herbal product. Rifampin: A medication commonly used to treat tuberculosis. Other medications may also alter the blood levels of omeprazole or vice versa. Always provide your healthcare provider with a complete list of medications you are taking or have recently taken.
